title: This is not your lasting home
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: The pauree begins by stripping this passing world of final status. It teaches that the way to the true dwelling is known through the Guru's Shabad, and that stable belonging is found in the company of the holy rather than in what cannot go with you.
whyItMatters: This one speaks to the person who feels unrooted, easily swayed, or hungry for real belonging. Taken seriously, it loosens attachment to what cannot last and directs the heart toward the company that steadies it.
takeaway: Do not mistake the temporary camp for your true home.

lines.gurmukhi: ਡਡਾ ਡੇਰਾ ਇਹੁ ਨਹੀ ਜਹ ਡੇਰਾ ਤਹ ਜਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddaddaa dderaa ih nahee jeh dderaa teh jaan ||
lines.translation: DADDA: This is not your true place; you must know where that place really is.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਆ ਡੇਰਾ ਕਾ ਸੰਜਮੋ ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: auaa dderaa kaa sa(n)jamo gur kai sabadh pachhaan ||
lines.translation: You shall come to realize the way to that place, through the Word of the Guru's Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਆ ਡੇਰਾ ਕਉ ਸ੍ਰਮੁ ਕਰਿ ਘਾਲੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: eiaa dderaa kau sram kar ghaalai ||
lines.translation: This place, here, is established by hard work,

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕਾ ਤਸੂ ਨਹੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਚਾਲੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kaa tasoo nahee sa(n)g chaalai ||
lines.translation: but not one iota of this shall go there with you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਆ ਡੇਰਾ ਕੀ ਸੋ ਮਿਤਿ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: auaa dderaa kee so mit jaanai ||
lines.translation: The value of that place beyond is known only to those,
upon whom the Perfect Lord God casts His Glance of Grace.
That permanent and true place is obtained in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy;
O Nanak, those humble beings do not waver or wander. ||29||

structure: The shabad says plainly that this visible place is not the soul's final dwelling.
From there it teaches that the way there is recognized through the Guru's Shabad, not through possession or effort alone.
It finally locates true stability in Saadh Sangat, where the heart stops wavering.
